---
title: "Installation"
---

Install phit with PIE:

```sh
pie install phpstats/phit
```

phit is a PHP extension, so it is installed once per PHP installation rather than per Composer project. Projects that cannot install extensions can use the [polyfill](extension-or-polyfill.qmd), which provides every function except the CSV reader.

## Requirements

| Requirement | Supported |
| --- | --- |
| PHP | 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5, non-thread-safe (NTS) builds. Thread-safe (ZTS) builds are not supported. |
| Operating system | Linux and macOS. Windows is not supported. |
| Installer | [PIE](https://github.com/php/pie), with `unzip` or PHP's zip extension to unpack prebuilt binaries |

## How PIE installs phit

PIE finds the latest release on Packagist, installs `phit.so` into the extension directory, and enables it for the PHP it runs under. To target another PHP installation, pass `--with-php-config=/path/to/php-config`.

- **Linux x86_64 and arm64 with glibc 2.35 or later:** PIE downloads a prebuilt binary. No compiler or Rust toolchain is needed.
- **macOS, Alpine and other musl systems, and glibc older than 2.35:** PIE builds from source. See [Building from source](#building-from-source).

## Building from source

The build needs these tools, which are not needed at runtime:

- `phpize` and `php-config` from the same PHP installation
- a C toolchain with `autoconf` and `make`
- stable Rust from [rustup](https://rustup.rs)
- Clang and libclang

On Debian or Ubuntu:

```sh
sudo apt-get install build-essential autoconf pkg-config \
  clang libclang-dev php-dev
curl -fsSL https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y
```

In the official `php:*-cli` images, PHP's development files are present. Add Clang, libclang, and the image's `$PHPIZE_DEPS`.

On macOS, install the Xcode command-line tools (`xcode-select --install`), Rust from rustup, and PHP and autoconf from Homebrew (`brew install php autoconf`). If the build cannot find libclang, the [development guide](development.qmd#environment) shows the variables that select Homebrew's LLVM.

## Prebuilt Linux binaries

Each [GitHub release](https://github.com/phpstats/phit/releases) has the binaries PIE uses. They are built on Debian Bookworm for NTS, non-debug PHP, and can be installed by hand. The names follow this pattern, shown for v0.5.0:

| PHP | x86_64 | arm64 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8.3 | `php_phit-v0.5.0_php8.3-x86_64-linux-glibc-nts.zip` | `php_phit-v0.5.0_php8.3-arm64-linux-glibc-nts.zip` |
| 8.4 | `php_phit-v0.5.0_php8.4-x86_64-linux-glibc-nts.zip` | `php_phit-v0.5.0_php8.4-arm64-linux-glibc-nts.zip` |
| 8.5 | `php_phit-v0.5.0_php8.5-x86_64-linux-glibc-nts.zip` | `php_phit-v0.5.0_php8.5-arm64-linux-glibc-nts.zip` |

Each archive holds `phit.so`, `INSTALL.txt`, a `manifest.json` with the build environment and minimum glibc, the license, and the third-party notices. A `.sha256` file sits beside each archive.

```sh
f=php_phit-v0.5.0_php8.4-x86_64-linux-glibc-nts
sha256sum -c "$f.sha256"
unzip "$f.zip" -d phit
sudo cp phit/phit.so "$(php-config --extension-dir)/"
```

Then add `extension=phit.so` to the PHP configuration of each runtime that needs it, and restart PHP-FPM.

## Verify

```sh
php -r 'echo phpversion("phit"), PHP_EOL;'
```

The command prints the installed version, such as `0.5.0`.

The command line and PHP-FPM often read different configuration files. Check the web runtime separately, for example with `extension_loaded('phit')` in a request. Restart PHP-FPM workers after installing or upgrading. [Deploying to servers](deployment.qmd) covers containers and FPM.

## Declare the dependency

Declare the extension in composer.json so that Composer reports a missing extension at install time:

```json
{
    "require": {
        "ext-phit": "*"
    }
}
```

The polyfill also satisfies `ext-phit`. See [Extension or polyfill](extension-or-polyfill.qmd).

## Upgrade

Run `pie install phpstats/phit` again, or replace `phit.so` with the newer binary, then restart PHP-FPM. The [release notes](https://github.com/phpstats/phit/releases) and the [changelog](https://github.com/phpstats/phit/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) describe each release.
